items.title: The Clashing Pair
items.question: Cognitive dissonance theory holds that holding inconsistent beliefs — or acting against beliefs — produces real psychological discomfort.
items.correctExplanation: True. Inconsistency hurts: minds strain toward coherence, and the strain motivates change. Discomfort is the theory's engine.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Festinger's core claim is affective, not just logical: contradiction feels bad, and feeling bad moves minds. Comfort demands consistency.
items.lessonContent:
Contradiction feels bad before thinking starts.
Strain motivates changes logic cannot.
Coherence comforts more than truth does.
Discomfort engines all dissonance effects.
Share this: notice one clash aching.

items.title: The Dollar Gap
items.question: In Festinger and Carlsmith's classic study, participants paid $1 to lie about a boring task later rated it MORE enjoyable than those paid $20.
items.correctExplanation: True. Twenty dollars justified lying externally; one dollar forced internal justification — attitude followed. Less pay, more persuasion of self.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The $20 group blamed the money; the $1 group, lacking cover, convinced themselves. Insufficient justification moves attitudes that ample bribes leave parked.
items.lessonContent:
Small rewards move attitudes most.
Cover lacking forces internal rewrites.
Bribes park what pennies persuade.
Justification scales inversely with pay.
Share this: justify one dollar task.

items.title: The Thin Excuse
items.question: Dissonance effects grow strongest when external justification for an act is minimal — big excuses leave attitudes untouched.
items.correctExplanation: True. Ample excuses absorb inconsistency externally; thin ones force internal revision. Justification and attitude change trade off exactly.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Large bribes and threats explain acts away, sparing beliefs; crumbs of justification leave minds to reconcile alone. Thin cover, thick change.
items.lessonContent:
Thin cover forces thick change.
Excuses absorb what attitudes would carry.
Trade-offs govern justification effects.
Crumbs persuade; banquets merely pay.
Share this: act on thin excuse once.

items.title: The Big Bribe
items.question: Larger financial rewards for saying something you disbelieve produce proportionally larger shifts in your actual belief.
items.correctExplanation: False. Big rewards explain the act away — no dissonance, no shift. Bribery scales inversely with persuasion of self.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Twenty dollars buys compliance while sparing conviction; one dollar buys conviction by starving excuses. Persuasion of self needs poverty, not wealth.
items.lessonContent:
Wealth excuses; poverty persuades selves.
Bribery scales against belief change.
Conviction needs thin justification.
Paid minds stay put inside.
Share this: resist one big excuse.

items.title: The Harsh Welcome
items.question: Aronson and Mills found that volunteers enduring severe initiation to join a dull group later rated the group MORE favorably.
items.correctExplanation: True. Effort justification: suffering for entry must mean the group is worth it. Ordeals inflate affection reliably.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Severe-initiation subjects loved the dull discussion; mild-initiation ones shrugged. Minds price memberships by pain paid, not quality received.
items.lessonContent:
Pain paid prices memberships highly.
Ordeals inflate affection reliably.
Suffering for entry must mean worth.
Effort justifies what reason wouldn't.
Share this: value one hard-won group.

items.title: The Easy Door
items.question: Groups that admit members effortlessly inspire the deepest loyalty and highest ratings from joiners.
items.correctExplanation: False. Costless entry breeds indifference: without suffering to justify, affection stays flat. Easy doors open onto lukewarm rooms.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Mild-initiation controls rated dull groups dully: no pain, no price inflation. Loyalty needs investment to feel valuable.
items.lessonContent:
Costless entry breeds indifference reliably.
Flat affection follows painless joining.
Investment creates value feelings.
Easy doors open lukewarm rooms.
Share this: earn one membership dearly.

items.title: The Spread Choice
items.question: After difficult decisions, people rate chosen options higher and rejected ones lower than before choosing — the spreading of alternatives.
items.correctExplanation: True. Choice creates dissonance; spreading resolves it: winners gilded, losers tarnished post-decision. Deciding rewrites desirability.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Brehm's appliances proved it: post-choice ratings diverge from pre-choice ones systematically. Minds flatter decisions already made.
items.lessonContent:
Decisions rewrite desirability after the fact.
Winners gilded, losers tarnished routinely.
Choosing creates the dissonance spreading cures.
Minds flatter their own verdicts.
Share this: catch one spread happening.

items.title: The Failed Prophecy
items.question: When a cult's doomsday prophecy failed publicly, Festinger observed believers proselytizing harder rather than dispersing.
items.correctExplanation: True. Disconfirmation plus public commitment plus social support produced intensified faith: 'When Prophecy Fails' documented it. Failed dates recruit, given sunk belief.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The Seekers' saucer never landed — and members preached more fervently after. Public commitment plus effort converts disproof into recommitment.
items.lessonContent:
Disproof converts the heavily invested.
Public commitment blocks graceful exits.
Failed dates recruit under sunk belief.
Effort defends what evidence attacks.
Share this: update one failed belief.

items.title: The Shattered Flock
items.question: Failed prophecies invariably destroy religious movements, scattering followers permanently in every documented case.
items.correctExplanation: False. Prophecy failure sometimes intensifies movements (Seekers, Millerites' remnants): conditions decide, not failure alone. Dispersal is one outcome among several.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. History shows recommitment, reinterpretation, and schism alongside collapse: failure's effects depend on commitment, support, and leadership. Invariably is always wrong here.
items.lessonContent:
Failure's effects depend on conditions.
Recommitment rivals collapse historically.
Invariably claims fail most reliably.
Prophecies fail; movements adapt variously.
Share this: study one survived failure.

items.title: The Buyer's Glow
items.question: After expensive purchases, buyers rate their chosen product higher and rivals lower than beforehand — post-decision spreading in showrooms.
items.correctExplanation: True. Costly choices demand justification: owned items gild, rejected rivals tarnish. Receipts rewrite ratings reliably.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Post-purchase spreading is showroom dissonance: money spent must mean value gained. Buyers remorse less by esteeming more.
items.lessonContent:
Receipts rewrite ratings reliably.
Owned items gild post-purchase.
Costly choices demand flattering follow-ups.
Remorse fades where esteem grows.
Share this: catch one buyer's glow.

items.title: The Unmoved Chooser
items.question: Difficult decisions leave people's evaluations of the options essentially unchanged — attitudes stay frozen through hard choices.
items.correctExplanation: False. Hard choices move evaluations most: near-ties generate maximum dissonance, maximum spreading. Difficulty drives revision, never stasis.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Easy choices barely ripple; agonizing ones reshape preferences deeply. Frozen attitudes contradict decades of spreading data.
items.lessonContent:
Agony reshapes preferences deeply.
Near-ties generate maximum revision.
Difficulty drives change, never stasis.
Frozen attitudes contradict the data.
Share this: feel one choice reshape you.

items.title: The Forced Smile
items.question: Acts performed under heavy coercion generate maximum dissonance, since the helplessness stings most sharply.
items.correctExplanation: False. Coercion supplies complete external justification — no dissonance at all. Guns explain acts fully; attitudes rest undisturbed.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Forced compliance needs no internal revision: the gun accounts for everything. Dissonance requires felt choice, however slight.
items.lessonContent:
Guns explain acts too completely.
Felt choice, however slight, is required.
Coercion spares attitudes entirely.
Helplessness stings without dissonating.
Share this: choose slightly, feel fully.

items.title: The Cool Observer
items.question: Bem's self-perception theory offered a rival account: people infer attitudes from behavior dispassionately, with no discomfort required.
items.correctExplanation: False as a full replacement — Bem's account explains some findings elegantly but arousal evidence (misattribution studies) proves real discomfort operates. Rivals coexist; neither monopolizes.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Self-perception handles low-arousal cases neatly, yet physiological evidence shows genuine discomfort driving classic effects. Both mechanisms live in the literature together.
items.lessonContent:
Rivals coexist in mature literatures.
Arousal evidence proves real discomfort.
Elegance never monopolizes explanation.
Both-and beats either-or here.
Share this: feel one theory working.

items.title: The Trivial Clash
items.question: Any inconsistency, however trivial and consequence-free, generates full-strength dissonance regardless of outcomes or self-relevance.
items.correctExplanation: False. Cooper and Fazio showed dissonance needs aversive consequences plus felt responsibility: trivialities fizzle. Stakes and ownership gate the effect.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Mismatched socks cognitions change nothing because nothing matters and nobody chose. Consequences plus responsibility are entry tickets.
items.lessonContent:
Stakes gate effects reliably always.
Trivialities fizzle without consequences.
Ownership plus outcomes open the gates.
Mismatches need mattering to move.
Share this: shrug one trivial clash.

items.title: The Minor Mirror
items.question: Threats to trivial self-images — being once slightly late, misplacing keys — produce the strongest dissonance effects of all.
items.correctExplanation: False. Aronson showed dissonance strikes hardest at central self-conceptions (competence, morality), not trivia. Mirrors crack over core reflections.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Lateness and keys barely register; cheating and cruelty detonate. Self-concept centrality scales the blast.
items.lessonContent:
Centrality scales every blast radius.
Trivia tickles; core threats detonate.
Mirrors crack over core reflections.
Competence and morals matter most.
Share this: guard one core reflection.

items.title: The Smoker's Library
items.question: Smokers commonly reduce quit-pressure by disputing evidence, citing long-lived smoking relatives, and postponing action to someday.
items.correctExplanation: True. Classic dissonance management: attack the cognition that quitting is urgent. Libraries of excuses shelve the same fear.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'Inconclusive evidence,' 'grandpa smoked,' 'I'll quit Monday' — the canon of smoked reasoning. Dissonance writes extensive apologetics.
items.lessonContent:
Apologetics shelve identical fears widely.
Excuse canons share structures globally.
Disputing evidence soothes cheapest.
Someday postpones every reckoning.
Share this: shelve one excuse permanently.

items.title: The Prompt Quitter
items.question: Learning about smoking risks makes the large majority of smokers quit promptly without further struggle or delay.
items.correctExplanation: False. Knowledge rarely suffices: most smokers continue, managing dissonance instead of behavior. Information informs; addiction and habit decide.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Decades of warnings coexist with persistent smoking: facts lose to rationalization routinely. Quitting needs more than knowing.
items.lessonContent:
Facts lose to rationalization routinely.
Knowing rarely suffices for quitting.
Information informs; habits decide.
Warnings coexist with persistence.
Share this: act on one known fact.

items.title: The Mind Denial
items.question: Meat eaters tend to deny minds to food animals while granting rich inner lives to pets — the meat paradox in action.
items.correctExplanation: True. Bastian's work shows moral status tracks menus: edible minds shrink, pet minds expand. Categories serve appetites.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Pigs lose smarts while dogs gain souls in eaters' ratings — motivated mind-perception. Appetites sculpt ontologies conveniently.
items.lessonContent:
Appetites sculpt ontologies conveniently.
Menus sort minds, not just meals.
Categories serve stomachs silently.
Denied minds ease full plates.
Share this: grant one food animal mind.

items.title: The Pledge Price
items.question: Fraternity hazing severity predicts later member loyalty and alumni giving — harsher pledging, tighter brothers.
items.correctExplanation: True. Effort justification in Greek letters: suffering for brotherhood must mean brotherhood is precious. Pledges price loyalty in bruises.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Hazing research mirrors the lab: severe initiations bind tighter than mild ones. Bruises become bonds through dissonance arithmetic.
items.lessonContent:
Bruises become bonds through arithmetic.
Severity binds tighter than kindness.
Prices paid inflate prizes won.
Pledges purchase loyalty in pain.
Share this: earn one bond gently instead.

items.title: The Fleeing Flock
items.question: Everyone subjected to painful initiations abandons such groups at the first opportunity, since suffering repels rational joiners.
items.correctExplanation: False. Sufferers disproportionately stay and praise: dissonance converts pain into devotion. Rational joiners are the first to re-enlist.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Pain predicts persistence, not flight: the harsher the welcome, the warmer the remembered home. Leaving would waste the suffering already spent.
items.lessonContent:
Pain predicts persistence paradoxically.
Suffering spent demands devotion returns.
Harsh welcomes warm remembered homes.
Flight would waste invested agony.
Share this: question one paid-for loyalty.

items.title: The Easy A
items.question: Students value effortlessly earned A's more than grades wrested through struggle — ease of victory sets attachment levels.
items.correctExplanation: False. Wrested grades glow brighter: effort inflates worth just as initiations inflate groups. Easy A's spend lightly because they cost lightly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Struggle-bought grades outshine gifted ones in attachment studies. Effort prices achievement in classrooms exactly as in cults.
items.lessonContent:
Struggle-bought grades outshine gifted ones.
Effort prices achievement universally.
Wrested glows brighter than granted.
Classrooms replicate cult arithmetic.
Share this: earn one grade the hard way.

items.title: The Cold Calculation
items.question: Sunk-cost persistence reflects pure forward-looking calculation with no backward-looking discomfort about wasted investments.
items.correctExplanation: False. Waste-aversion aches: abandoning investments admits loss, and dissonance prolongs projects past reason. Calculators with feelings keep digging.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Forward math says quit; quitters flinch at admitting waste. Dissonance funds failing projects that calculation would shutter.
items.lessonContent:
Calculators with feelings keep digging.
Admitting waste aches worse than wasting.
Feelings fund failing projects steadily.
Forward math loses to backward ache.
Share this: quit one sunk project cleanly.

items.title: The Averted Headline
items.question: People selectively avoid news, books, and arguments that would clash with their existing commitments.
items.correctExplanation: True. Selective exposure manages dissonance preemptively: unread challenges can't clash. Avoidance is dissonance insurance.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Readers dodge dissonant headlines; viewers curate comforting feeds. Preemptive avoidance beats post-hoc rationalization for economy.
items.lessonContent:
Avoidance beats rationalization economically.
Unread challenges never clash at all.
Curated feeds are dissonance insurance.
Preemption manages cheapest of all.
Share this: read one clashing headline.

items.title: The Preacher's Mirror
items.question: Preaching a virtue and then recalling personal lapses reliably moves behavior toward the sermon — the hypocrisy paradigm in action.
items.correctExplanation: True. Aronson's hypocrisy induction works: advocated standards plus remembered failures equal changed conduct. Mirrors held after sermons convert.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Condom-sermon plus lapse-recall increased real safer behavior: dissonance between pulpit and practice resolves toward pulpits. Preaching binds preachers first.
items.lessonContent:
Pulpits bind preachers before audiences.
Lapses recalled convert sermons lived.
Mirrors held after preaching work.
Advocacy plus memory equals change.
Share this: preach one virtue, then practice.

items.title: The Private Choice
items.question: Dissonance effects require deliberately lying to other people — purely private choices, unwitnessed, never generate dissonance.
items.correctExplanation: False. Private decisions dissonate fully: spread-of-alternatives needs no audience. Solitude stages dissonance perfectly well.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Choosers alone still gild winners and tarnish losers: no witnesses required. Audiences amplify; privacy suffices.
items.lessonContent:
Solitude stages dissonance perfectly well.
Audiences amplify what privacy suffices.
Unwitnessed choices still spread wide.
No lying needed for clashing.
Share this: decide one thing privately well.
